`urllib.parse.urlsplit()` splits a URL into five components: scheme, netloc, path, query and fragment. `urllib.parse.urlunsplit()` reverses it. It takes any five-item iterable, such as the tuple `urlsplit` returns, and combines it into a complete URL string. The result may be a slightly different but equivalent URL if the original had redundant parts, such as an empty query. `urlparse` and `urlunparse` are the six-component variants, which add `params`.
